question: Why are North rentals down on last year since May?
answer:
# Why North on-rent days are down year on year since May

**Short answer:** The North fell behind last year from the week the new North list prices went live (4 May 2026). This data can't prove the price change caused it, but nothing else in the data explains the timing. The gap comes less from 2026 falling and more from 2026 staying flat while 2025 climbed through May and June.

## The timing

| Fiscal wk | 2026 week | 2026 | 2025 | Change | % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 06 Apr | 4,704 | 4,764 | −60 | −1.3% |
| 2 | 13 Apr | 4,464 | 4,586 | −122 | −2.7% |
| 3 | 20 Apr | 4,704 | 4,666 | +38 | +0.8% |
| 4 | 27 Apr | 5,007 | 4,770 | +237 | +5.0% |
| 5 | **04 May (new prices)** | 4,686 | 4,676 | +10 | +0.2% |
| 6 | 11 May | 4,494 | 5,193 | −699 | −13.5% |
| 7 | 18 May | 4,933 | 5,030 | −97 | −1.9% |
| 8 | 25 May | 4,642 | 5,185 | −543 | −10.5% |
| 9 | 01 Jun | 4,931 | 5,069 | −138 | −2.7% |
| 10 | 08 Jun | 4,638 | 5,532 | −894 | −16.2% |
| 11 | 15 Jun | 4,787 | 5,672 | −885 | −15.6% |
| 12 | 22 Jun | 5,038 | 5,451 | −413 | −7.6% |

- **Weeks 1–4 (before the price change):** 18,879 vs 18,786, which is **+0.5%**. Essentially level with last year.
- **Weeks 5–12 (from the price change):** 38,149 vs 41,808, which is **−3,659 days (−8.8%)**.

## It's every North depot, not one

| Depot | Wks 1–4 change | Wks 5–12 change |
|---|---|---|
| D01 Hollin Cross | −82 (−1.1%) | −1,430 (−8.4%) |
| D02 Petherby | +150 (+2.8%) | −863 (−7.3%) |
| D03 Scarrow Bridge | +25 (+0.4%) | −1,366 (−10.6%) |

All three depots turned negative at the same time. That points to a cause that applies to the whole region rather than a local problem at one site. The North price change applied to all categories (ACC, EAR, PWT, PWL, CON) in all three depots.

## What supports the price explanation

- **Timing:** Rentals were flat against last year until the new list went live on 4 May. The gap opens the following week.
- **Customer feedback:** On 19 May, Petherby reported regulars "grumbling about the new prices," with two saying they'd shop around.

## What rules out other explanations

- **Missing data:** None. No North weekly files are missing for this period, so this isn't a gap in the data.
- **Other staff notes:** The Carrick Stowe closure, the Tidesend walkout and the forklift renewals are all in the West and South regions. None of them touch the North.

## The important nuance

2026 hasn't actually dropped. North averaged about 4,720 days a week in weeks 1–4 and about 4,770 in weeks 5–12. Last year went from about 4,700 to about 5,230 (+11%) over the same stretch. So the real question is **why the usual May–June seasonal lift didn't happen this year**.

There are two possible readings, and this data can't separate them:
1. The price rise suppressed the seasonal pick-up.
2. 2025's lift was unusually strong (weather, a large project), and 2026 is closer to normal.

## Suggested checks to confirm

- **South as a comparison:** South raised prices on 6 April, four weeks before the North. If South on-rent days dipped against last year from mid-April, that strongly supports a price effect. If they didn't, look elsewhere.
- **Earlier years:** Get North data for May–June 2024 to see whether 2025's lift is the normal pattern.
- **Revenue, not just days:** If the North price increase was roughly 10% or more, revenue may be flat or up despite 8.8% fewer on-rent days. That changes whether this is a problem.
- **Category and customer mix:** Check whether the drop is concentrated in particular categories or among regular accounts, which the Petherby note hints at.
